segments.title: Quiet signals in political change
segments.summary: A favourite lesson from history is to look past the loud spectacle of unrest and notice the quieter choices that can shift political power.
segments.body: Political upheaval does not always make its greatest threats obvious. People shouting in the streets and creating a visible disturbance may command attention, yet governments may need to worry more about quiet actors making consequential decisions out of sight. A personal analogy sharpens the point: a loud noise usually signals that something is happening, while a barely audible sound may be a threat approaching unseen. Speech works the same way. Omissions can carry as much meaning as spoken words, either because the words are unnecessary or because the person talking has read the room carefully. Together, the examples show why quiet behavior and silence deserve attention alongside public rhetoric.
segments.question: What is your favourite lesson from history?
segments.answerShort: Quiet developments can matter more than loud ones. During political upheaval, watch the people and decisions operating out of public view, and notice what speakers leave unsaid.

evidence.note: The answer contrasts noisy revolutionary protest with quiet actors and explains why omissions in speech can be meaningful.
